구.forms: Sino-Korean · dates, money, minutes, phone numbers, floors (구 층, 구월)
구.t: Homonym: 구 also means a city district, e.g. 강남구.

카메라.x: I took a lot of pictures with my new camera.

이메일.x: I sent an email to my teacher.

동쪽.x: The sun rises in the east every morning.
동쪽.t: Koreans list compass points as 동서남북, "east-west-south-north," not north-south-east-west.

부지런하다.ex: 우리 할머니는 아침 일찍 일어나시는 부지런한 분이에요.
부지런하다.x: My grandmother is a hardworking person who gets up early in the morning.
부지런하다.t: 부지런하다 means busy and active; for steady, honest effort, Koreans prefer 성실하다.

책가방.ex: 아이가 무거운 책가방을 메고 학교에 가요.
책가방.x: The child goes to school carrying a heavy school bag.

한테서.forms: Same form after any person or animal; casual (often shortened to 한테)
한테서.x: Yesterday, on my birthday, I got a present from my younger sibling.
한테서.t: Use 한테서 for people and 에서 for places: 친구한테서, 학교에서.

행동하다.ex: 생각만 하지 말고 이제 직접 행동하세요.
행동하다.x: Don't just think about it; take action yourself now.

최소한.forms: 최소한 + amount: 최소한 한 시간 · 최소한의 (+noun)
최소한.ex: 하루에 최소한 물을 여덟 잔은 마셔야 해요.
최소한.x: You should drink at least eight glasses of water a day.

벌이다.m: to start, launch, hold (an event); to spread out
벌이다.ex: 시청에서 환경 보호 캠페인을 벌이고 있어요.
벌이다.x: City Hall is running an environmental protection campaign.
벌이다.t: Don't mix it up with 벌리다 'to open wide': 입을 벌리다 'open your mouth'.

종합.ex: 다음 주에 종합 건강 검진을 받을 거예요.
종합.x: I'm getting a comprehensive health checkup next week.

성과급.ex: 올해는 회사 실적이 좋아서 성과급을 많이 받았어요.
성과급.x: The company did well this year, so I got a big performance bonus.

신문사.x: My uncle works as a reporter at a newspaper.

게시물.x: That post got a lot of comments.
게시물.e: Literally 'thing put up to show', like a notice on a board.
게시물.t: In casual speech people often just say 글 or 게시글 for an online post.

객관성.x: It is important for the news to maintain objectivity.
객관성.e: Literally 'a guest's view'; -성 = '-ness/-ity': 객관성, 공정성, 신뢰성.
객관성.t: Pronounced [객꽌썽] — both 관 and 성 are tensed.

전문의.ex: 정확한 진단을 위해 전문의에게 진료를 받으세요.
전문의.x: See a specialist for an accurate diagnosis.
전문의.t: Pronounced [전무늬]; specialists name their field, e.g. 피부과 전문의 'dermatologist'.

법칙.x: Newton discovered the law of gravity.
법칙.t: 법칙 is a law of nature or science; laws made by a government are 법 or 법률.

염치없다.x: I hate to impose, but please help me just one more time.
염치없다.t: 염치없지만 is a humble opener meaning 'I'm embarrassed to ask, but…'.

거꾸로.forms: 거꾸로 + verb (거꾸로 입다/들다); 거꾸로 말하면 = conversely
거꾸로.m: upside down, backwards, inside out; the other way around
거꾸로.ex: 동생이 옷을 거꾸로 입고 학교에 갔어요.
거꾸로.x: My little brother went to school with his clothes on backwards.
거꾸로.e: Related to the verb 거꾸러지다 'to fall headlong'.

가슴이 답답하다.m: to feel frustrated and stifled; to have a tight chest (lit. the chest feels stuffy)
가슴이 답답하다.ex: 아무리 설명해도 이해를 못 하니까 가슴이 답답해요.
가슴이 답답하다.x: No matter how much I explain, they don't get it, and it's so frustrating.
가슴이 답답하다.e: 답답하다 is the closed-in feeling of a stuffy room: worry or frustration seems to block the chest.
가슴이 답답하다.t: Pronounced [가스미 답따파다]. Also a physical symptom: tell a doctor 가슴이 답답해요 for chest tightness.

배심원.x: The jurors decided that the defendant was not guilty.
배심원.e: Literally 'members who sit in on the judging'.
배심원.t: In Korea's citizen participation trials, the jury's verdict is only advisory, unlike in the US.

협박.ex: 그는 돈을 주지 않으면 비밀을 말하겠다고 협박했어요.
협박.x: He threatened to tell the secret if he wasn't given money.
협박.t: Pronounced [협빡]; the verb is 협박하다, and the victim takes -을/를.

회의론.ex: 그 계획에 대해 회의론을 제기하는 사람도 있어요.
회의론.x: Some people are raising skepticism about that plan.
회의론.t: This 회의 means 'doubt', not 'meeting'; 회의적이다 means 'to be skeptical'.

동경.x: I've longed for city life since I was a child.
동경.t: Its homonym 동경 is the old Korean name for Tokyo.

협정.ex: 두 나라는 자유무역 협정을 맺기로 합의했습니다.
협정.x: The two countries agreed to sign a free trade agreement.
협정.e: Literally 'settled together' — terms fixed by mutual agreement.
협정.t: Common verbs: 협정을 맺다, 협정을 체결하다 (sign), 협정을 파기하다 (scrap).

빚다.m: to cause, to bring about (trouble, confusion); to shape, to make (dumplings, pottery)
빚다.ex: 새 정책이 시민들 사이에서 혼란을 빚고 있습니다.
빚다.x: The new policy is causing confusion among citizens.
빚다.e: Literally 'to shape by hand' (만두를 빚다) — problems get 'shaped' too.
빚다.t: News pattern: 혼란/갈등/차질/물의를 빚다 'cause confusion/conflict/setbacks/a stir'.

추켜세우다.m: to praise highly, to extol; to raise up (straight)
추켜세우다.ex: 언론은 그 영화를 올해 최고의 작품으로 추켜세웠습니다.
추켜세우다.x: The press hailed the film as the best of the year.
추켜세우다.e: 추키다 'to lift up' + 세우다 'to stand up': lifting someone up high.
추켜세우다.t: Interchangeable with 치켜세우다 in the 'praise' sense; both often hint the praise is exaggerated.

반제품.ex: 이 공장은 반제품을 수입해서 완제품으로 만들어요.
반제품.x: This factory imports semi-finished goods and turns them into finished products.
반제품.e: Literally 'half-made product'. 반- = half: 반값, 반제품.

디딤돌.x: I will use this failure as a stepping stone to success.

울타리.m: fence, hedge; protective shelter, safe circle (figurative)
울타리.ex: 부모님은 언제나 저의 든든한 울타리가 되어 주셨어요.
울타리.x: My parents have always been a reliable protective shelter for me.
울타리.e: Literally a fence around a house; figuratively the people or system that protect you.

형사소송.x: In criminal proceedings, the prosecutor must prove the crime.

경상수지.x: Last month's current account posted a surplus of 5 billion dollars.

교향악단.ex: 이번 주말에 교향악단의 정기 공연을 보러 가요.
교향악단.x: This weekend I'm going to see the symphony orchestra's regular concert.
교향악단.t: Often shortened in names: 서울시향 is short for 서울시립교향악단.

혹평하다.ex: 평론가들은 그 영화의 지루한 줄거리를 혹평했어요.
혹평하다.x: Critics panned the movie's boring plot.
혹평하다.t: 혹평을 받다 'to be panned' is very common; the opposite is 호평을 받다.

허투루.forms: 허투루 + 쓰다/듣다/보다, usually with 않다 or 말다: 허투루 듣지 마세요
허투루.ex: 할머니는 돈을 한 푼도 허투루 쓰지 않으세요.
허투루.x: My grandmother never wastes even a single penny.
허투루.e: Mostly appears in negative warnings, like 허투루 듣지 마 'don't take it lightly'.

통섭하다.m: to integrate, to unify (different fields of knowledge)
통섭하다.ex: 이 강의는 인문학과 과학을 통섭하려는 시도입니다.
통섭하다.x: This course is an attempt to integrate the humanities and science.
통섭하다.e: Literally 'unite and encompass'; popularized as the Korean term for E.O. Wilson's 'consilience'.

옹색하다.e: Literally 'blocked and clogged' — no room to move.
옹색하다.t: Common: 옹색한 변명 'a lame excuse' and 살림이 옹색하다 'to be hard up'.
